title: A playground of joy
credit: Katie Cloyd, Romper (2023). Sponsored by Stapelstein®. Adapted source.
context: A sponsored parenting advertorial. Work with one of the first four body paragraphs; the headline, byline and sponsorship remain part of the context.
prompt: Choose one narrative or language choice in one of the first four body paragraphs. What does it do in this sponsored article?
transcript:
romper                                                                                      MENU

PARENTING Sponsored by STAPELSTEIN®

The Product That Transformed
My House Into A Playground
Of Joy, Just In Time For The
Holidays

One box opened up a world of open-ended play.
by
KATIE CLOYD


Fall2 and winter can be a challenging time for parents trying to keep our kids active and
entertained. The crispness in the air is refreshing, but when the skies are gray and the sun sets
early, we need to find ways to stay inside without squelching the magic and wonder of these
precious childhood days.

It was barely the crack of dawn when my children’s giggles and squeals filled my home with
palpable excitement. I tried to be cranky about the early awakening, but I was unsuccessful. There
is nothing like the wild abandon of unbridled childhood laughter — especially when the joy is
radiating from your own children.

I was pretty sure I knew what had delighted my children into waking before the sun. I descended
the stairs to the family room to find my children playing with the Stapelstein stacking stones I’d left
out for them as a surprise the night before.

As I entered the room, my seven-year-old was busy hopping from one “stone” to another. My
oldest was trying his luck balancing on the Board. The youngest had laid her head on a red
element as if it were a pillow and was pretending to sleep.

Stapelstein translates from German to English literally as “stacking stones.” The company was
founded by designer Stephan Schenk and his partner Hanna König in an effort to help kids
embrace open-ended, active play and to bring families together in a new way. The Rainbow
Classic Set I’d put out for my kids includes six brightly colored Original stones.

You may find copycats online, but trust that these simply do not compare. Original Stapelstein
pieces are made of eco-friendly EPP (expanded polypropylene) and produced in Germany in a
climate-neutralized process. They’re also non-toxic, eco-friendly, recyclable, and water, bite, and
saliva-resistant (IYKYK)3, with each piece having undergone a patented laser surfacing process
that enhances durability and smooths the surface so it’s easy to wipe clean.

While the design is minimalist and attractive enough to feel like décor in your family room, it’s also
incredibly durable, with each stacking stone weighing only 0.4 lbs4 but capable of holding up to
395 lbs5. Original Stapelstein elements are truly designed to endure for generations of play.

As my kids played, the floor turned to lava. Then it was the ocean. Elements were stacked
two high, then three. Rainbow order. Reverse rainbow order. Flipped over to make a bed for a
tiny plush elephant. Filled with invisible pirate treasure. Served up as bowls of soup. Worn like
funny hats.

My husband even joined the play, declaring the “river rocks” were slippery with algae and
pretending to slip on the green stone and fall into the “creek” in an extremely exaggerated fashion.
The kids roared with laughter as he pretended to splash and swim on the family room floor.

As the morning wore on, the Stapelstein elements made their way into every game my kids
decided to play. My husband and I retreated into the kitchen to make pancakes, and the sounds of
the kids’ imaginations continued to fill the house with joy.

I fell in love with Stapelstein that day. One simple, colorful stacking stone set provided an avenue
for discovery, cooperation, and joy for an entire glorious morning for all three of my kids—with no
screens or tech in sight. I also love that I don’t have to worry about where to store them. They’re
gorgeous, they stack beautifully, and the stacks can even be used as dynamic stools to sit at the
table and eat or color.

We can’t wait to expand our collection. With three weeks off of school during the months of
November and December, my family will have every opportunity to discover all the things that
Stapelstein can become, turning weeks that might have felt like being “cooped up” into cozy
cherished memories.

In this modern world where kids are inundated with noisy, complicated toys, games, and
experiences that give them a pre-determined script and set of rules, Stapelstein provides kids
with a chance to just play. The simple design, unmatched durability, sustainable materials, and
company core values make Stapelstein a playroom and holiday gift list must-have. They’re the
perfect addition to your child’s world of imagination and creativity.



1
advertorial: also known as “native advertising” in the U.S.
2
fall: another word for “autumn”
3
IYKYK: stands for “If You Know, You Know”
4
0.4 lbs (pounds): 0.18 kg (kilograms)
5
395 lbs (pounds): 179 kg (kilograms)

title: A manifesto for the future
credit: Gate Theatre, “A Manifesto for our Future” (n.d.). Adapted source.
context: A manifesto on the website of a London theater company. Read the introductory context, then choose one of its four sections.
prompt: Choose one section and one language pattern. How does that pattern contribute to what the theater asks of its readers? Use at most two brief quotations.
transcript:
About our Manifesto
The Gate has existed for over 40 years. As well as celebrating the trailblazing artists who began their
careers here, we want to look ahead to what the next 40 years and beyond might require of us.
A Manifesto for our Future is a way to shout about the things we believe in, and declare the things we
want to be held accountable for. We want it to be a celebration of our values and a starting point for
change. And we hope it will be a way to hold complexity and nuance, and to imagine possible futures.



A MANIFESTO FOR OUR FUTURE
PROCESS IS POLITICAL
It is relevant who makes the work.
Amplify the voices silenced by the canon*.
Text is not the only form of authorship.
Our artists are international.
Our shows are multilingual.
Our rehearsals are open.

FORM IS POLITICAL
Look outside what you know.
Rethink definitions of excellence.
Celebrate subjectivity.
Celebrate the mess and imperfection of humanity.
Celebrate liveness.

OUR WORK IS PART OF THE WORLD
Acknowledge and hold the suffering of the past.
Imagine the future.
Don’t portray the world, change it.
We are nature and nature is us.
There must be space to come together and talk.
We declare a climate emergency.

CHANGE. TRANSITION. TRANSFORM
Make work in a circular economy (and only 20 % of materials can be new).
The shows (and all the conversations too) must leave the building.
Texts from earlier than 2010 must be radically interrogated.
At least one show in every season must be made outside the UK.
Everyone in the room is part of the show (this includes the audience).
We can’t do this without you.
What happens after the play is the point of the play.




* canon: a widely agreed upon set of rules or standards
